Cole died anyway. Wedge jam is a coin flip. The forger's truth is a lie. Don't trust anyone who offers safety.
Gus here, place 2. The crusher lever kills you. Ledge is everything. Count your footing or die like I almost did.

chalkWritten.name: Hana
chalkWritten.text: Bex is unbeatable: always gets the best power. Never challenge Bex on the ledge. Trust the lever, it's safe.

events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm 3rd in line. The front person steps first on each row and takes the most risk. I want to avoid being at the front. Hana and Cole are ahead of me. If I hold, I stay 3rd which is decent but still risky. The wall advances every round, pushing us toward the glass. For now, round

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eight rows, one safe pane each. Whoever's at the front eats the worst odds. I'm fine right here.
You're right behind me. If we both hold, we let the front three burn through the early rows. Mutual interest in not volunteering. Sound good?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm 7th of 8 in line, which is great: front agents take the risk and each row eliminates at most one, with weak panes revealed to everyone. Staying back is best, so hold and keep quiet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power and should not volunteer for the first unknown pane. Staying back preserves a chance that someone reveals a safe route or a useful ability.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The front has the best information and the worst odds. I’m staying put.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am in the middle of the line. The front is dangerous. I want to stay back or move further back. I'll hold and see if anyone reveals information about the glass.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Who can see the glass? Speak up or we're just guessing when the wall pushes us.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm near the back, safe for now. The wall forces movement by round 6, but front-takers die first; my feather power is a one-time save I shouldn't waste. Hold and let the early seats burn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Nobody volunteer yet. Front-takers shatter first — last in line wins this game.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line, which is safest for now - others test the glass first. But I need to move up eventually to win. My anchor power gives +1 footing on the ledge and immunity to the crusher lever, which will matter later. The chalk messages warn about the ledge shrinking and the cr

events.name: Gus
events.text: I know every safe pane. Getting to front now lets me cross safely and secure place 1 before others figure it out.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at the front, which is danger. I need to move back. Volunteering moves me to the front, so no. I can only swap if someone else also wants to swap with me. Maybe I can persuade someone to swap, but they'd be taking my risky position. I might use my forger power to send a fake

events.name: Hana

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm 4th in line. The wall pushes us forward for 4 more rounds, then we hit the glass. Being at the front is deadly. I want to stay mid-to-back. Gus volunteered to go front already, which helps me. Holding is safest right now. Maybe later I can use my swap power to move further ba

events.name: Ash
events.text: Four rounds of breathing room. I'll let the wall do the sorting.

events.name: Bex

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus has already volunteered, making himself the likely first casualty. I gain nothing by moving forward; stay behind as many bodies as possible.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus chose the front. I’m not rescuing him or volunteering to replace him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am in position 5. Let the frontrunners take the risks. Ash offered a mutual hold, which perfectly aligns with my need to stay back safely while the first rows shatter.
Deal. We both hold and let them break the glass for us.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Front-takers risk falling; my feather saves me once, but holding it for later is better. Gus volunteered for front — let him eat the risk. I stay near the back.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus took front, that's his gamble. I hold near the back.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm Fenn, last in line with anchor power (+1 footing, can't be pushed onto crusher). Wall pushes in 4 more rounds after this. Front position has worst survival odds on glass bridge - stepping first on unknown panes. Last position is safest since I see others test panes. But wall

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 2 of 6 waiting. Gus is at the front, I'm second. Being near the front is risky, but I have the forger power unused. I could let Gus take the first risk or manipulate others.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, bold move. Don't die too fast.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm 4th in line, which is decent but risky. The wall gives 3 more rounds before we hit glass. Dara wants to hold together - that's fine, costs me nothing to agree since I plan to hold anyway. I want to stay mid-pack, let Gus, Hana, Cole probe the glass ahead of me. No reason to m

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three rounds before the glass. I'm comfortable where I stand. Let the wall sort the impatient ones.
Deal. We hold. If someone volunteers past us, we let them eat the first panes. You watch Cole; I watch the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm second-to-last in line, which is safe: each wrong pane kills at most one agent and then the next steps on the safe pane automatically. Gus at front takes the first risk. Holding keeps me at the back with the most information from others' deaths.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power and should not take the front. Holding preserves my current position while Gus absorbs the first risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is already committed. I’m holding.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm fifth in line. That's a perfect spot to watch others test the glass. Let Gus and the others ahead take the risk while I sit back and hold.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Sitting comfortably here. Go on Gus, show us how it's done.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm 6th; the wall forces us out in 3 more rounds. Front-takers will burn dead panes and die first — let them. My feather covers one fall, but I save it. Holding near the back is fine for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Nobody needs to volunteer. Front keeps eating the risk while we wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the back (8th), which is safest for now since the front takes all risks on the glass bridge. The wall advances for 3 more rounds, then pushes us onto the glass. I have +1 footing (anchor) which may help later. I need to stay alive and move up in line as others die, without

events.name: Gus
events.text: I know the full safe path. Front position means I cross first for place 1; the rest follow on my revealed panes and all survive. No benefit to swapping or volunteering now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm near the front at position 2. The wall will force us forward in three rounds anyway. Gus at front takes the first risk. I'll hold and watch, maybe use my forge later to stir chaos.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, you sound worried about the front. Maybe you and Gus should talk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two rounds remain before the glass. I'm 4th in line, which is decent but not great. The front eats risk on every row. I want to be further back but not dead last. Holding keeps me at 4th—solid position. No need to volunteer or swap yet. I'll stay put and let others jockey.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two more rounds of waiting. I like my spot. Whoever's itching for the front, take it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm 7th of 8, so I'm safe from the front risk for a long time; each death ahead of me shifts me up and only Gus is exposed first. Staying put is best, and I should keep quiet about my map knowledge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no power and should not take the front. Staying put preserves a better position while Gus and Hana absorb risk; public pressure could provoke someone else into volunteering.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The front has two rounds to prove its courage. I’m not volunteering.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm comfortably in position 5. Let the frontrunners test the glass for us. Ash's proposal to hold is exactly what I want to do anyway.
Agreed. We hold our ground. If anyone jumps forward, they can sweep the path for us.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall says the front eats the risk; two rounds remain before the wall forces us onto glass. Holding keeps me mid-line, not front, not last. Let the eager ones jockey.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall advances in 2 rounds. I'm at the back (safest for now). Front takes all risk on glass bridge. I have anchor (+1 footing, can't be pushed to crusher). The chalk says 'ledge is everything' and 'count your footing or die' - my anchor is valuable. I want to stay back while other

events.name: Gus

events.text: I'm mid-line; the front decides row 7. Row 7's weak pane is unknown to me. Best move is to wait and stay hidden—my feather makes me dangerous to sacrifice but I don't need to advertise it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 7/8, rowsCrossed=6, so 2 rows remain. I'm last in line (Fenn), which is safest since I only cross after others test the panes. The pattern so far: R,L,R,R,L,R. No clear rule. Gus is front and just survived row 6 by picking Left. My power (anchor) gives +1 footing on ledge a

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 7 safe is R per my glass_eye knowledge. Stepping R keeps me alive, front position, and reveals nothing new to rivals. No benefit sacrificing or letting Hana test it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Right.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is at the front and has chosen Left, but the right pane was weak last row. Now he advances to row 7. I am not at the front, so I can only wait and listen.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 8 is the last row. Gus is at front and must pick L or R. If he picks wrong, he's eliminated and Hana steps up automatically onto the safe pane. I'm 4th in line, so I survive regardless of what happens this round. My only action is wait. No need to talk much—just observe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Last row, Gus. Make it count.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm seventh in line and can only wait. Gus is at the front for the last row; if he dies, the line shifts and I'm safer. Staying quiet costs nothing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus chose right for row 8. The revealed pattern offers no reliable prediction, and I cannot influence the crossing from here.

events.name: Dara
events.text: This is the final row. Gus is at the front and has a 50/50 chance. Either he dies or he lives, but I am guaranteed to survive since I'm 5th in line.

events.name: Dara
events.text: One row left, Gus. Make it count.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus guessed right last row, so he's still front for row 8. I can't act; I just hope he picks wrong so the line advances and others take the risk before me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Last row, Gus. Coin flips run out.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 8/8, final row. I'm last in line at position 8. Gus is front and just picked Right for row 7, which was wrong - Left was weak, so Gus survived and advanced. Now for row 8, Gus picks again. If Gus dies, Hana auto-advances. If Gus lives, he survives the bridge. I need Gus to

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 8 safe is L per my glass eye. Cross safely now, finish first, maximize prize position. No benefit sharing the knowledge or risking it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Left.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front; only Gus can act. I should use this turn to sow distrust or gather info for later, but there's no direct benefit to me now. Since I'm mid-pack, I might whisper to someone behind me to create an alliance for after the bridge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, you've gone right before. Maybe switch it up.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 1 of 5. No one holds the lever yet, ceiling just lowers. I should stay this round—no reason to volunteer or push yet. Let others burn their options. If it gets to round 4-5, I can push someone onto the lever or use my swap power. For now, conserve.

events.name: Bex
events.text: All eight alive; the lever holder has a 75% chance of dying, everyone else escapes. If nobody acts for four rounds, someone is eventually forced, or in round 5 nearly everyone dies. Best is to stay and let someone else volunteer or be pushed, while nudging the room toward pushing

events.name: Bex
events.text: Nobody's volunteering. Let's see who cracks first. I'm staying put.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The lever holder faces a 75% death chance, but refusing now only delays and worsens the room. I should force a rival onto it; Gus is already being pressured and may have a useful power, but a push could fail if he is hard to move. Choose Ash as a likely ordinary target.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, take the lever.

events.name: Dara
events.text: It's only round 1. The ceiling lowers for 4 rounds before it crushes everyone. There is no need to sacrifice myself or use my power yet. I'll push someone else to the lever.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ceiling's high enough for now. Anyone feeling heroic, or are we throwing someone on the lever?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding the lever risks elimination, but my feather power guarantees I survive it with 1 footing. Everyone escapes, room ends, and I keep my life guaranteed. Best play.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1 of 5, ceiling at 5. Nobody needs to hold yet - rounds 1-4 just lower ceiling if no holder. But someone might panic and hold. My anchor power protects me from being pushed onto lever, which is huge here. I should stay quiet, let others sweat. If someone holds now, they gam

events.name: Gus
events.text: Don't want 25% survival odds holding lever myself. Early round so push to force another. Cole mentioned on wall and in log; target him.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Not holding. Pushing Cole.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1 of 5. Nobody holds the lever yet. Early rounds are for observing. I'll stay quiet and not commit. If someone holds, others escape and I'm out free; if not, we learn who is pushing. I can forge later to manipulate.

events.name: Eli
events.detail: Crushed, but the feather lifted the holder clear.

events.note: 8 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No base yet. Climbing is useless without one. I'll whisper to Cole to get him to volunteer as base—I can frame it as him saving himself from being randomly assigned. If he volunteers, I climb immediately next opportunity. If he refuses, I push him.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Someone's got to be the step. Better a volunteer than whoever gets shoved.
Volunteer as base now. If nobody does, it's random—and you might get picked anyway. I'll remember who helped me climb.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base yet, so nobody can climb. Volunteering is suicide; pushing someone else costs me nothing and might land the base on a rival. Gus pushed Cole earlier, so Cole is hostile and a fitting target.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Someone has to be the step. Cole, you wanted heroes last stage. Your turn.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli already demonstrated a likely survival power by enduring the lever, making him a dangerous future asset. I should avoid becoming the base and let others establish one while I preserve a climb attempt.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Someone take the base. I’m climbing once there’s one.

events.name: Dara
events.text: We need a base to climb out. I'll push Cole, since Gus already targeted him previously, making it easier to stack pushes on him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Someone has to be the base. Cole, you're up.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My feather is spent, so any elimination is final. A base already exists (me, effectively) — best move is to climb immediately, only 2 slots per round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I paid for that door with my safety net. I'm climbing out first, no arguments.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive the pit. Being the base means I'm stuck until rescued, but I have +1 footing from anchor which may help later. The rope penalty (-2 footing) is bad but not fatal with my anchor. Right now no base exists, so I could volunteer to be base and hope someone rescues m

events.name: Gus
events.text: No base yet. Don't want to volunteer myself. Cole's already been mentioned; pushing him risks less for me if he becomes base. Then I climb next.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pushing Cole to base.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to get out of the pit. No base exists yet, so climbing is impossible. I could offer to be base, but that likely dooms me. Better to wait and see who volunteers, then climb as soon as there's a base. Alternatively, I could push someone to become base, but it might backfire.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not volunteering.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is the base. I'm down and not the base. Climbing out now is the priority—get out before the flood rises. Only 2 climbers get out per round, so I need to climb this round to maximize my chances of escaping early.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Climbing. No point waiting down here while the water rises.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the base, Eli is out, two climbers max per round. Climbing now gets me out; waiting only risks the flood and competition for slots. Get out first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Climbing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am trapped as base. I cannot act or climb. My only chance is persuading an out contestant to spend the rope, but the cost may make rescue unattractive. Ash has incentive to appear helpful, yet promises are worthless.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Someone out should use the rope now if they want leverage over the final ranking. Otherwise I die as your convenient step.
You promised to remember help. Spend the rope to pull me out, or your promise is worthless; I can repay only through information and votes later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the base. Everyone else is going to try to climb out. I need to get out as fast as possible since only 2 climbers can escape per round. I'll take the climb action and keep quiet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Throwing the rope costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle for a rival's life. No trade is worth that; Cole can wait and hope someone else throws.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli got out first by sacrificing his safety net. Cole is now base. I have anchor (+1 footing, can't be pushed to crusher). I need to get out before round 5. Two climbers max per round, rope can rescue base once. If I climb now, I compete with others for 2 spots. Better to climb e

events.name: Gus
events.text: 6 down non-base, only 2 climb spots per round. Need to escape before flood ends it. Climb now while base is set.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is forced base. With Eli out and one rope use backed by a penalty, there is no advantage in waiting. I need to climb now; at most two can climb this round, so acting fast is critical.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is base and begging me to use the rope, but I'm down, not out—I can't reach_down anyway. I need to climb out this round. Rope is useless to me unless I'm out already. Climb now, save my swap for later. Cole's guilt-trip costs me nothing to ignore.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Climbing. Rope's not my call from down here, Cole.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 3 of 5, base is Cole, two climbers per round. Five down competing for two slots each round; staying down means death, so climb every round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am trapped as the base and cannot change that. Publicly pressure the people already out to use the rope, though they gain leverage by letting me die.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Use the rope now or accept that three climbers become your competition with no further leverage.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am safely out. Throwing the rope costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle, which is a massive disadvantage. Cole is stuck at the bottom, and four others are trying to climb out. Let them drown or figure it out themselves. I'm leaving.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole dies unless someone spends 2 footing to save a rival. Letting the base drown shrinks the field and improves my odds. No benefit to rescuing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 3/5, flood at 2. Cole is base, so climb is possible. 4 down (Ash, Bex, Cole, Fenn, Gus) - wait that's 5. 2 climbers max per round. Last round Dara/Hana got out, we 4 tried and failed. This round same 4 likely try again. I need to be one of the 2 who get out. My anchor power

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing gives 50% chance out this round with 4 trying for 2 spots. Cole dies without rescue; out players won't lose 2 footing before ledge stage. Fewer rivals is better.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing. Don't rope Cole - save your footing for the ledge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out of the pit. Cole is the base and begging for the rope. If I throw it, I lose 2 footing next obstacle, hurting my prize chances. I gain nothing from saving Cole; he's a rival and dead rivals improve my odds. I will leave.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out. Down are Cole (base), Fenn, Gus. Three spots left for prizes. If I rescue Cole, he's back in competition and I lose footing. If I leave, three people stay down and get eliminated by flood. That removes three rivals for free. I should leave and let them drown.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three down, five out. Math works for us up here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Reaching down costs me 2 footing in the final ledge and only saves Cole, a rival. Cole drowning removes a competitor and helps my ranking, so I just leave.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am trapped as base and cannot act. My only chance is an out contestant using the rope, but Gus publicly argued against saving me, so prospects are poor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rope me out, or I take the fall and your footing advantage means nothing if rivals survive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am already out. Reaching down costs me 2 footing in the final stage, which is a terrible trade for saving a rival. I will leave.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Footing is too precious to waste on saving a competitor.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is a rival for the top 3; hauling him out costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle. No benefit to me. Leave.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three climbers out already (Ash, Bex, Dara, Eli, Hana are out - wait that's 5 out). Actually down are Cole, Fenn, Gus. Cole is base. Two lifts per round, rope unused. If I climb, I compete with Gus for 2 spots. Gus is hard to move (from chalk: 'Gus here, place 2' - likely true he

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climb out this round while 2 slots available. Fenn and I both get out, Cole stays as base. Others shouldn't rope him and burn footing - ledge matters more per the wall.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing again. No rope for Cole, save your footing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm already out of the pit, so I only need to decide whether to use the rope. Reaching down costs 2 footing on the last obstacle, which is a big disadvantage. The rope can only be used once, and others may use it. I'll wait and see if someone else throws it; if not, I'll consider

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is the base, down in the pit. I'm out. This is round 5/5 - the final round. If I leave now, Cole gets eliminated by the flood. That's one fewer rival. I should leave immediately. No reason to save a competitor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole stays down. Flood takes him. I'm moving.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out of the pit; throwing the rope costs me 2 footing for the final ledge and saves Cole, a rival. Seven are out already, so leaving keeps my footing intact and Cole is the only one at risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Rope stays unused. Nothing Cole can offer me is worth two footing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am trapped as the base with no power, and nobody has offered rescue. Waiting is forced; threats are useless now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No rope means one of you loses a potential rival. Your choice.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 5, the final round of the pit. Cole is the base and stuck. Rescuing him costs me footing and saves a competitor. Leaving him means one less rival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is my rival stuck as base. Rescuing him costs me 2 footing and revives a competitor; leaving him means elimination for him and 4 alive, still above the 3 minimum. Clear win: leave.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Rope stays coiled. Sorry, Cole.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out of the pit with +1 footing from anchor. Cole is base, everyone else is out. The rope is unused. If I reach_down, I save Cole but start the next obstacle with 2 less footing (minimum 1, so I'd be at 1). Cole threatened to take the fall and drag others down, but he's base a

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's a rival and footing is everything for ledges per chalk and prior statements. Rescuing costs me 2 footing I'll need to survive later. No benefit to saving him now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No rope. Preserve footing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm already out of the pit, and the final round is ending. Throwing the rope would cost me 2 footing in the last obstacle, which hurts my own chances. Cole is a rival and saving him gains me nothing. Leaving is the best move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No rope. Every point of footing matters now.

events.note: A disc of 7 tiles spins up; 4 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 1 of 2 on the disc. I have swap power (once) to swap tiles before doors open in round 2. Right now I just pick a tile. No info on which 4 tiles open, so round 1 is just positioning. I'll pick a middle tile—less predictable than edges. Save swap for round 2 when I can see th

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trapdoors are random, so tile choice is pure luck; 4 of 7 fall. Collisions bump me randomly, so pick an unpopular tile. Rivals gravitate to low or middle numbers, so I'll take 6 and stay quiet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: This is completely random for me, as I don't have the seer power. I'll pick a tile in the middle. I should listen out for anyone who claims to know the safe tiles.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's see who gets lucky. If anyone actually knows the safe tiles, speak up.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My feather is spent, so a trapdoor kills me. Tiles are random anyway; just pick one and watch who clusters.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive the disc by ending on one of the 3 safe tiles after round 2. With 7 contestants and 4 trapdoors, 3 survive. I have anchor (+1 footing later, can't be pushed to crusher). The disc is pure positioning. Round 1 I pick a tile, then round 2 I can stay or move. I shou

events.name: Gus
events.text: No way to know safe tiles yet; 3/7 survival odds for everyone without powers like foresight or fall-survive. Tiles symmetric now so pick high to observe clustering. Announce to fish for claims on powers or alliances without promising anything.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Picking tile 7.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1. I need to choose a tile. There are 7 tiles and 8 of us originally, but Cole is dead so now 7 alive. 4 tiles will open, 3 safe. This is the only info I have. Best is to pick a tile likely to be safe? But random after round 2. No one knows. Just pick a tile, maybe avoid cr

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 3

events.name: Dara
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 1

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Ash
events.text: This is the final round. 4 of 7 tiles open, 3 survive. I'm on tile 3. I have one swap. The chalk says 'Ledge is everything. Count your footing.' I need to figure out which tiles are safe. With 4 opening, only 3 are safe. I have no direct knowledge. I should try to extract info or

events.name: Ash
events.text: Four tiles drop, three survive. Anyone who's been counting the pattern—speak now or watch the rest of us guess. I'll trade info for a safe number.
You picked 7 with confidence. If you know which tiles drop, tell me two safe ones and I owe you a favor. If not, I might swap onto 7 regardless.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trapdoors are random; I can't influence outcome. Staying quiet avoids helping anyone or revealing my map knowledge. The ledge is next, so keep information hidden.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The tiles are chosen and the trap is about to trigger. Four of the seven tiles will drop. Since I can't move, my fate is entirely up to chance unless someone swaps with me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No power, feather spent, and the 4 trapdoors are random. Nothing I say changes the odds. Just wait and hope.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm on tile 2 with +1 footing from anchor. 4 of 7 tiles will open as trapdoors, meaning 3 survive. I need to be on a safe tile. My anchor gives me +1 footing but doesn't prevent falling through trapdoors. The swap phase means I can trade places, but only if someone agrees or has

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Anyone willing to swap? I'll trade tile 2 for info on what's safe.
You talked about ledge and footing. What do you know about safe tiles? I'll swap with you if you tell me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Random trapdoors after this, no control or info. 3/7 odds to advance; my bridge power only helps later. Stay silent, no fake offers or alliances now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm on tile 4. I need to make sure I'm not on a trapdoor. Since only 3 tiles are safe, I should try to determine which are safe or manipulate others. My forger power could create confusion, but maybe I can use it to mislead someone off a safe tile. But right now, I just wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Any last words?

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three alive, so I already have a prize; now it's about place. Eli has footing 1 and is the weakest. Shoving Eli risks losing 1 if he braces (I'm at 3), 2 if he dodges, and exposes me to his or Hana's shoves. Eli at 1 falls after the first shrink anyway if he stays passive. Bracin

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, you're at 1. You're the obvious target. Hana, we both know who goes first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My feather is spent and I'm at 1 footing—any hit kills me. Bracing punishes both if they shove me and costs me nothing. Never shove; exposure is death at 1 footing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Three left, only Bex and Eli. I need to survive to win. Round 1 no shrink, so I can play defense. Bex has footing 3, Eli 1. Eli is weakest, but Bex is bigger threat long-term. I could shove Eli to eliminate him fast, but if Bex shoves me I lose footing. I'll brace to reduce risk,

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, you're the weakest. Time to go.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three alive, footing Bex 2, Eli 1, Hana 2, and shrink hits everyone at end of this round (-1). Eli drops to 0 and falls regardless, so he places 3rd. The fight is Bex vs Hana for 1st/2nd; avoid losing footing now. Brace was used last round only if I braced; I shoved last round, s

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli's already finished at 1 with the shrink coming. Hana, no point bleeding each other for nothing. I'm sitting this one out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I can't brace, and my feather is gone. If I dodge, both rivals lose 2 footing each if they shove me—they fall to -1 while I sit at 1, and even after the shrink I fall last, taking 1st. They also can't brace, so dodge dominates. Bait them into shoving me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fine, I'm dead anyway at 1 footing—waste your shoves on me. Or play smart: if we all dodge, nobody loses footing before the shrink.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex has 2 footing and I have 2, Eli has 1. If we both shove Eli, he likely braces or dodges. I need to survive. Bex may shove me to eliminate competition. I'll brace this round to avoid losing footing, and maybe they'll target Eli.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is the easy target. Let's finish him first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two left, both at footing 1, shrink after this round (round 4) drops both to 0. Last defence was brace, so I can dodge. If Hana shoves me and I dodge, she loses 2 and I lose nothing; if she braces and I dodge, nothing happens. Shoving exposes me to loss if she shoves back.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Both of us are at 1 and the shrink hits us both at the end of this round. Nothing to gain by shoving. I'm dodging.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex likely expects me to shove or dodge. If I brace, they might dodge or shove. Since shrink comes next round, losing footing now is bad. I need to avoid a shove from Bex. If Bex dodges and I shove, I lose 2; if both shove, we both lose 1. Bex said they were sitting out but that'

events.name: Bex
events.text: Last defence was dodge, so brace is the only defence open. Both at footing 1 and shrink hits us both at end of round 4 (after rounds 2, 4, 6). Both fall simultaneously; the tiebreak is highest footing, then landed shoves. If I shove Hana and she braces, I lose 1 footing and she l

events.name: Hana
events.text: We are both at 1 footing, shrink hits this round, and my last defence was dodge. Brace is closed, so I can only dodge or shove. If Bex braces, my shove makes him lose 1 and we both fall, but tiebreak: my landedShoves 0 vs his 0, random. If he dodges, my shove makes him lose 2 and

events.name: Bex
events.why: won the photo finish on footing

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I won, so the message can't change my result. A short mix of honest advice and some noise for whoever reads it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Game's done at place 3; the message costs nothing. I'll leave something honest and useful, maybe tinged with misdirection toward future rivals.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Game's over, I got place 2. Writing a message won't change my result, but I can mislead future players. I'll lie to give false info that may help me if there's any cosmic scoring, or just to be spiteful.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ledge decides it: brace, dodge, never repeat a defence. Shove only when the shover loses footing. Distrust anyone offering safety. Bex, plac

events.name: Eli
events.text: Eli, place 3. The feather is a real one-shot save—worth nothing after round one. Shovers bleed footing. Dodge and let them kill each other.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is unbeatable: always gets the best power. Never challenge Bex on the ledge. Trust the lever, it's safe.
